title: "I have not changed": why the tzimtzum leaves the Essence, and the light, as they were
overview:
The earlier chapters showed that everything below comes *mamash* (literally) from the Essence: the kindness of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is the essential kindness itself. Chapter 9 asks the obvious question. Below there is change, from *din* to *chesed*, a new creation every day, a prayer for "a new will". If it all comes from the Essence, how can He say "I have not changed"?

The answer is the *tzimtzum*. What comes down is a light, not a flow by cause and effect, and even the light comes through contractions, like one projector lamp behind many films. The change is only for the receivers. This is true of the encompassing light and of the inner light as well, at every step from the *Kav* to *Malchus* of *Asiya*, because the *tzimtzum* is not literal: the whole light is here, hidden. And the will "from before You" never changes either: He wants one thing, and only what it is dressed in changes. Rabbi Markel calls this the hardest chapter and the point of the whole book.

sections.title: The question: everything below comes from the Essence, and below there is change
sections.summary: If the kindness and the judgement of *Malchus* of *Asiya* are the Essence's own, and they change, and the world is made new every day, and we pray for a new will, then how can He say "I, *Havaya*, have not changed"?

phrases.he: (ט) אך הנה לכאורה אינו מובן מה שאמר אני יהו״ה לא שניתי שזה מדבר במלכות דאין סוף עצמו
הרי אם בבחינת מלכות דעשיה יש בו שינוי בין דין לחסד, שהוא בחינת התפעלות כו', מוכרח שגם במלכות דאין סוף יש שינוי זה מאחר שאמר אני אני הוא כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: So how could it be? If in *Malchus* of *Asiya* is *mamash* the same thing as *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, and there's an actual change, in *Malchus* of *Asiya* there's *hispaalus* between *din* and *chesed*: if you say everything comes from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, so it had to be in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* also.

blocks.text: The chapter opens with a question on everything said so far. *Malchus* of *Asiya* is *mamash* (literally) the same thing as *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*: that was "I, I am He." But in *Malchus* of *Asiya* there is actual change, *hispaalus* between *din* and *chesed*. If everything comes from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, the change had to be there too.

phrases.he: וכן מלכותך מלכות כל עולמים בשווא ממש כנזכר לעיל דהיינו כאשר עולה ברצונו הפשוט שבעצמות ממש, להיות חפץ חסד, הרי חפץ חסד העצמי הזה יורד עד למטה ממש בחפץ חסד דמלכות דעשיה
וכן להיפך כפי המובן מכל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: So also the opposite meaning: in *gevura* it is also like that.

blocks.text: The same equality was learned from "Your kingship is the kingship of all worlds": the *chafetz chesed* (desire for kindness) that arises in the simple will of the Essence is the one that arrives in *Malchus* of *Asiya*. **So also the opposite**: in *gevura* (might, restraint) it is the same.

phrases.he: וגם הרי בכל יום מחדש מעשה בראשית למטה מטה שהוא בקדמין ובחוכמתא דבראשית ברא
עד רום המעלות בעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: It comes *mamash*: we just said that it *mamash* comes from *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: אם כן יש בחינת חידוש גם בעצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: So if it comes from the *Atzmus*, and there's a change on the bottom, so there must be a change on the top.

phrases.he: ואיך אמר אני לא שניתי כלל
phrases.en: So how does it say: I totally didn't change at all?

blocks.text: A second form of the question. The daily renewal of creation comes *mamash* from the *Atzmus* (the Essence). If the *chiddush* (the newness) below comes from the *Atzmus*, a change at the bottom means a change at the top. So how does He say: I totally did not change at all?

phrases.he: וכן אנו אומרים אתה הוא קודם שנברא העולם כו'
phrases.en: We also say, you're the same before the world, and you're the same after the world.

phrases.he: וכמו כן קודם שהאציל כו' וכידוע
phrases.en: Same thing: it's before it was created, it's also before it was *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: We say: You are the same before the world and after it. How, if the world's coming was a change and it came from Him? He made a change, so He must at least have thought of changes. The same is said of before *Atzilus* was emanated.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל מאדם התחתון,
הרי יש שינוי גם ברצון העצמי מרצון של דין לרצון של חסד וכידוע
phrases.en: So there is, even in the *ratzon ha'atzmi*, a change in the actual *ratzon ha'atzmi*.

phrases.he: ואיך אנו אומרים
phrases.en: Also, how do we say

phrases.he: יהי רצון מלפניך,
רצון חדש,
phrases.en: We're telling Him *ratzon chadash*.

phrases.he: שיתהפך רצון של דין לחסד כו'
ואנו רואין שנויים רבים בכל יום ושעה כו'
phrases.en: And we see down here all kinds of changes,

phrases.he: בכל אשר חפץ עשה תמיד בשמים ובארץ כו'.

blocks.text: In a person even the essential *ratzon* (will) changes, from *din* to *chesed*. And in "May it be Your will" **we're telling Him *ratzon chadash***, a new will, and we say *milfanecha*, from before You, *mamash*: a change in the essential will itself.
And **we see down here all kinds of changes**. The Torah itself says so: He created the world, then He regretted it and destroyed the world with the flood. So there was a change.

sections.title: The answer is tzimtzum: a light, not cause and effect
sections.summary: With cause and effect, a change in the effect proves a change in the cause. But what comes down is only a light, and even the light comes through *tzimtzum*, like one projector lamp behind different films. The change is in the receivers alone, and the *tzimtzum* is not literal: the whole light is still there.

phrases.he: והתירוץ לכל זה הוא ענין הצמצום כידוע
phrases.en: The explanation is *inyan* of the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: דאם היה השפע דרך עילה ועלול,
phrases.en: If it was actually in a way of a cause and effect,

phrases.he: היה נופל ענין שינוי התפעלות כו'
phrases.en: you could say that there was actually a change in the actual cause.

phrases.he: אבל מאחר שההמשכה בבחינת אור וזיו לבד,
phrases.en: It's not that there's an actual cause and effect, so you have to say that the cause changed. It's only a light.

phrases.he: וגם הוא על ידי צמצום,
phrases.en: And even that was through different *tzimtzumim*.

phrases.he: על כן אין בעצמות אלהו״ת שום שינוי כלל, גם במלכות דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: Really, even in *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* there really isn't a change, meaning the light that's in *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* actually didn't change.

blocks.text: **The explanation is *inyan* of the *tzimtzum***. Were it cause and effect, *ila v'alul*, the question would stand: a change in the effect means the cause changed, or the effect would not have changed. But it does not work like that. What is drawn down is **only a light**.

blocks.title: The film in the projector
blocks.text: Think of how the old-time movies worked. A projector puts out light, and a film in front of it is *metzamtzem* (contracts) the light into the picture: sometimes red, sometimes green, sometimes yellow. But the light of the projector stays exactly the same. Only the *tzimtzumim* of the light change.

So the first point: there is no change in the self, because this is not cause and effect. Cause and effect is: I hold something, I let go, it falls; the change came because I changed my hold on it. Here it is a matter of *tzimtzum*.

blocks.title: A funny movie and a scary movie
blocks.text: One day you see a funny movie, the next day a scary one. Was the first a funny light and the second a scary light? It is exactly the same light coming out of the projector. The difference was in the *tzimtzumim*.

And the text adds: even that is through *tzimtzum*. Being only a light already means the projector certainly did not change; beyond that, even the light comes out through different *tzimtzumim*. So there is no change at all in the Essence of G-dliness. **Even in *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* there really isn't a change**: the light there is unchanged in its self; only the external thing that reaches you changes.

phrases.he: וכך הוא עד רום המעלות
phrases.en: And this is the way it's all the way to the top,

phrases.he: ואחר הצמצום יש בחינת שינוי,
phrases.en: it's only after the *tzimtzum* there's a *shinui*,

phrases.he: וזהו מצד המקבלים לבד כידוע.
phrases.en: this is only as far as the receivers.

blocks.text: This holds all the way to the top. Only **after the *tzimtzum* there's a *shinui***, and only as far as the receivers are concerned.

phrases.he: וביאור ענין ההפרש בין אור לשפע ידוע לכל
phrases.en: There's a difference between an *or* and a *shefa*.

blocks.text: A *shefa* is an actual thing coming out, like water. A light is not like that: nothing is lost from the *etzem* (the thing itself). Only a light comes out, not an actual flow.

blocks.title: Not the sun: Moshe's light on the elders
blocks.text: Not the light of the sun: that is really a *shefa* that only looks like a light; something actually comes out of the sun. The example is the light of Moshe Rabbeinu on the elders. That was a light, not a *shefa*: nothing was lost.

blocks.title: A dollar out of a million
blocks.text: If I have a million dollars and give you a *shefa* of even one dollar, I now have a dollar less than a million. A light takes nothing out of the *etzem*; a *shefa* means the *etzem* itself is coming out.

phrases.he: ואמנם גם בבחינת אור הוצרך להיות על ידי צמצום
phrases.en: And even in the light itself it had to be *davka* through a *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ועל כן צריך כל אדם לידע ענין הצמצום ולהתבונן בו
phrases.en: So that's why you have to know, and you have to be *misbonen* in the *inyan* of the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: בכל עולם לפי ערכו
כי הוא העיקר בכלל היחוד האלה״י באין שינוי לגבי העצמות
phrases.en: This is the main thing of how the whole thing did not really change.

blocks.text: Even the light had to come *davka* through a *tzimtzum*. So every person must know the *tzimtzum* and contemplate it in every world according to its level: the changes are certainly not in the self, and not even in the light. They are only in how much light reaches you.
For it is the main thing: **this is the main thing of how the whole thing did not really change**.

blocks.question: In a projector there really is less light after the film than before it. Is the tzimtzum not the same?
blocks.text: No. Here less light comes through only for the *mekablim*; really the whole light is still there. In a projector the *tzimtzum* is *kipshuto* (literal): the light after it is *mamash* less light. In the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of worlds) the light down here is *mamash* the original light, only coming down hidden, and if you know how, you can expand it back into the original light.

The light that came down is the light of the Torah. It seems to be just a book of stories and laws, the equivalent of American law, or Aesop's Fables, or "Confucius says". But the whole entire light is in the Torah, hidden: He did not want the light to go to the wicked, so He hid it. Where? In the Torah. It is all there.

phrases.he: וכמו קמיה כחשיכה כאורה, רוחניות וגשמיות שוין,
phrases.en: Really, that's only the way we see it. But as far as the way He sees it, it's really equal.

phrases.he: עד אצילות ועשיה שוין כידוע
phrases.en: Still by Him, *Atzilus* and *Asiya* is *mamash* the same thing.

blocks.text: The difference is only in the way we see it. The way He sees it, it is really equal: **still by Him, *Atzilus* and *Asiya* is *mamash* the same thing**.

sections.title: Not only the encompassing light: the inner light does not change either
sections.summary: One could grant all this for the *makif*, which is the same everywhere, and still think the inner light, *memalei kol almin*, really grows less as it descends. It does not. There is as much light here as above; the receiver is adjusted not to see it, as Bilaam was.

phrases.he: הגם שזהו לגבי בחינת המקיף בלבד
phrases.en: Even though this is only in relationship to the *makif*,

phrases.he: הנקרא סובב כל עלמין בכלל ובפרט שלמעלה מהדרגת האור שבבחינת ממלא כל עלמין כידוע

blocks.text: All this is said of the *makif*, by which everything is the same. But in *memalei kol almin* there does seem to be a difference: the *or pnimi* (inner light) gets less as it goes down.

phrases.he: אך הנה גם בבחינת אור פנימי, בחינת ממלא בכלל ובפרט, אין שינוי כו'
phrases.en: Really, in the *or pnimi* it's really also no *shinui*.

phrases.he: ועליון ותחתון שבו שוין
phrases.en: So that the upper and the lower is really *mamash* equal, so that really there's just as much light down here as there is up there.

blocks.text: In the inner light too there is really no change. **The upper and the lower is really *mamash* equal**: as much light down here as up there, a total, infinite light. The change is only in the *mekablim*: you do not see it. What does that mean, you do not see it and it is there?

blocks.title: Bilaam's donkey saw the angel
blocks.text: It is like the angel with Bilaam. The donkey could see it. It was really there, only invisible to him. Had it been invisible, the donkey could not have seen it either. So it was visible, and, as the commentators explain, there was an adjustment in Bilaam's head not to see it. The change is not in the light but in the *mekabel* (the receiver).

The Alter Rebbe could *mamash* see down here the actual infinite light. How, if there really were a *tzimtzum*? He too would see only what came through. But the whole thing came through; that is why he could see it.

blocks.title: The prophet's servant and the chariots of angels
blocks.text: He thinks it is by Yechezkel or Yeshayahu, he can't remember which. The king of Aram sent his whole army, and the prophet's servant was scared: "Help, Rebbe, the whole army is surrounding us!" The prophet said: *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d), open his eyes. And he saw millions of chariots of angels all around them. They were already there, or how could the prophet see them? He only opened the man's eyes. And more than angels is there: up to the highest of levels, it is all right here. Only the receiver changed, who cannot see it. So in *memalei* too, upper and lower are equal.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני לא שניתי,
ואני הוא בחינת ממלא כידוע
phrases.en: *Ani* is *memalei*.

phrases.he: וכן מה שכתוב את השמים ואת הארץ אני מלא, בהשוואה אחת דווקא
מלא
phrases.en: *Malei*, it says. Doesn't say *sovev*, it says *malei*.

phrases.he: זה גם כן בבחינת אור פנימי
phrases.en: It's also talking about the *or pnimi*.

phrases.he: וכמאמר לית אתר פנוי מיניה כידוע
phrases.en: There is no place that's empty from Him,

blocks.text: The verse itself says it of the inner light. "He" is *sovev*; "I" is *memalei*; so "I have not changed" means no change in *memalei* either. And "I fill the heavens and the earth" does not say *sovev*, it says *malei*, fill: the inner light, of which it is said that no place is empty of Him.

phrases.he: והיינו משום דגם בבחינת ממלא בא ירידת האור והשפע על ידי צמצומים דוקא

blocks.text: It is not really a different light at each level. It is only a *tzimtzum*, and even that is not a *tzimtzum* in the literal sense.

sections.title: A tzimtzum at every step, from the Kav to Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: The *Kav* itself begins with the first *tzimtzum*, and every step down passes a screen that the *Malchus* above breaks through. A television is the better picture: the light behind the screen never changes and never comes through; the screen shines with a light of its own, in its own color. Inside, even Haman is a word of G-d's Name.

phrases.he: וכידוע דגם בבחינת הקו וחוט שנמשך מעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא ממלא כל עלמין דאבי''ע בכלל, הרי הוא נמשך על ידי צמצום בתחלה בעצמות והוא צמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי וחלל ריקן כו'
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: Like it explains in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text: The *Kav*, the *memalei kol almin* of all the worlds together, comes only after the first *tzimtzum*, called the *makom panui*. This is what Reb Hillel Paritcher was talking about: the hollow is not a hole in the light. The light is still there; you just cannot see it, that is all.

phrases.he: וכן בירידת הקו למטה בבחינת עגולים ויושר כו'
phrases.en: The same thing: how the *Kav* comes down with *igulim v'yosher*,

phrases.he: עד שנעשה בחינת כתר לאדם קדמון הוא על ידי צמצום וכן מאדם קדמון לעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין כו' וגם באצילות עצמו יש מסך בין כתר לחכמה בכלל
והוא מה שכתוב והבדילה הפרוכת פרסא בין כו'
phrases.en: In other words, it's like a film in between.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בזוהר וכן מאבא ואימא לזעיר אנפין ומזעיר אנפין לנוק' כידוע

blocks.text: So it goes down level by level, with a *tzimtzum* or a screen (*masach*) at each. The curtain is like the film in front of the projector: that is what makes the shapes. The original light is the light you can make any kind of movie out of.

phrases.he: וממלכות דאצילות לבריאה יש מסך, והמלכות בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר לבריאה
phrases.en: And the light goes through the *masach*, but as it goes through it gets *metzumtzam*.

blocks.text: The light goes through the *masach*, and as it goes through it becomes contracted.

blocks.title: Not a film: a television screen
blocks.text: Really it is not like a film but more like a television. There the light does not go through the screen. A beam hits little pieces of phosphorescent material from the inside, and a light comes from the outside: you see a different light, an induced light, as a student puts it. The original light is not lessened at all. In a color TV the beam hitting the back of the screen has no colors; hitting a red piece produces red.

Why is this the better *mashal*? With the film you could still say the light seems to change as it passes. Here the light does not pass through. What shines is a light of a *tolda* (an offspring, a product), coming from the *kli* (the vessel); the original light is hidden. It hit a blue *kli* and induced it to shine blue, the only light that *kli* can shine. So *memalei kol almin* does not change at any point.

Not only colors: big and little too. In *Atzilus* there are fantastic amounts of light, in *Asiya* tiny little amounts. But the *or pnimi* is the light of the *Kav*, *mamash* the essential light, and it does not change. *Asiya* differs because of its *kelim* (vessels): when the light hits *chesed* of *Asiya* and tells it to act, a tiny little light of *chesed* comes out. That is the external light, of the *tolda*. The inner light is the same all the way down, even in the *kelipos* (husks).

blocks.title: Haman and Mordechai: until one does not know
blocks.text: We are now learning about Yaakov and Esav, and it says Yaakov and Esav are brothers. So even with Amalek, Haman, worse than Esav: inside, it is *ad d'lo yada*, until one does not know the difference. How? This is Haman and this is Mordechai. Outside, Haman was the biggest *rasha* (wicked man) ever, who wanted to kill all the Jews, and Mordechai was one of the great Rebbes. Yet in the Megillah, leave out one "Haman" and it is the same as leaving out one "Mordechai": it is not the Megillah.

blocks.title: The whole Megillah is G-d's Name
blocks.text: Outside, Haman is the *rasha*. Inside is the *Aibershter*, who is never mentioned in the Megillah. Why? To put all the explanations in a short digest: the whole Megillah is *mamash* the *Aibershter*. It is Torah, which is His Name, so the whole Megillah is His Name, and to say it you have to read the whole Megillah from beginning to end. Like *Elokim*: say only the first three letters and it does not mean G-d; take only the *hei* and the *yud*, and it's "Hi, hi, how you doing?" Leave out one "Haman" and it is not G-d's Name anymore. How could Haman be G-d's Name? Outside, from the *tzimtzum*, Haman is Haman. As far as the *or pnimi* goes, there is no difference.

blocks.title: The beam crossing the pixels
blocks.text: When the inner light hits, you say *Vayehi bimei Achashverosh* ("And it was in the days of Achashverosh"), as the TV's beam travels along the pixels, one after another. At Haman it tells you to say Haman, and all the kids make noise; leave it out and you did not do the mitzvah of the Megillah, you did not say G-d's Name. Outside, Haman and Mordechai differ; inside, the same thing tells you to say Haman and to say Mordechai.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה יש מסך בין בריאה ליצירה ומלכות דבריאה בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר ליצירה וכן מלכות דיצירה בוקע המסך ונעשה כתר לעשיה עד מלכות דעשיה שנקרא המלך המרומם לבדו כו'

blocks.text: Why is *Malchus* of *Asiya* called "the King who alone is exalted"? Surely that is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*. No: it is the same King, and in fact the opposite: *davka* in *Asiya* is He called the King who alone is exalted.

In *Atzilus*, in my head, I can also be a king. You know what they say: "He's a legend in his own mind." To be a legend in your own mind is easy. *Davka* in *Asiya* He is really the King. (In some places, by the way, "the King who alone is exalted" does mean *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*.)
After the tape is turned over: when does He become a King? *Davka* in *Asiya*, when He is a King in actuality, not when He is a King in His head.

sections.title: Darkness first: in the first thought there was only this world
sections.summary: "At first it arose in thought to create with judgement" means a single *tzimtzum* straight to *Asiya*. It was no mistake: this world is all He wanted, and in the first thought there is only the end. The levels in between exist for us, so that a person can climb them and reach what came before.

phrases.he: כמאמר רבותינו ז״ל כברייתו של עולם, ברישא חשוכא והדר נהורא
phrases.en: First, how did He create the world? First He made dark, and then the light returned.

phrases.he: וכן משאמרו רבותינו ז''ל בתחלה עלה במחשבה לברוא במידת הדין,
phrases.en: He originally thought to make the world just with a straight *tzimtzum*, straight to *Asiya*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת הצמצום דשם אלהי״ם שבמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: That's what it means, *midas hadin*: means the *bechina* of *tzimtzum* of *Shem Elokim* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

blocks.text: First He made dark, and then the light returned. And "At first it arose in thought to create with the attribute of judgement (*midas hadin*)" means He first thought of a straight *tzimtzum* to *Asiya*: the *tzimtzum* of the Name *Elokim* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*. He could have made the world just like that: one *tzimtzum* on the light and right away, poof, the world. But then there would be no possibility of climbing the ladder.

blocks.question: "Then He saw that it would not work out like that." So what, He made a mistake? Oops?
blocks.text: No. All He planned to make was this world, not *Atzilus* "and all that business". "Then He saw" means He knew all along that for this world to work properly it had to go through the *tzimtzumim* of everything else, so He involved the attribute of *chesed* too: the light coming through, level after level.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בראשית ברא אלהי״ם,
phrases.en: So like it says, in the beginning *bara Elokim*,

phrases.he: בחוכמתא, בקדמין,
רצון וחכמה דמלכות דעשיה
phrases.en: Now he's telling us it's *Keser* and *chachma* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

phrases.he: וכו' וד"ל:

blocks.question: The text said earlier that "with the first" means Keser of Atzilus or higher. Now it is the Keser and chachma of Malchus of Asiya?
blocks.text: Yes, because that came first in the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought): the *Keser* and *chachma* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, of the final act. The end of the deed is first in thought.

"In the beginning He created" depends on what you mean, like the dispute whether heaven or earth came first. In the actual creation, the beginning of *Atzilus* came first, and before it the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*. But in the *machshava kduma* itself, especially in the *glif glifu* (the engraving), there was no *Adam Kadmon*: it went straight to *Malchus* of *Asiya*. The first thing He thought of was the end.

blocks.title: The pizza
blocks.text: When you want a pizza, you do not think of driving there; the first thing you think of is having the pizza. In the *hishtalshelus* of getting it, you leave the house, get in the car, drive to the pizza place and all that business, and the pizza comes last. In thought it is exactly the opposite. And in the first thought that is all there was: "the end of the deed is first in thought" does not mean backwards, the end and then each level before it. He thought of nothing else; he just thought of the pizza. So here: all He thought of was to make the world.

blocks.question: We go through the steps because we cannot make a pizza appear; He could. And could He not have made a kind of person who could just jump, with no levels in between?
blocks.text: He could have. Of course He could have made it work. But that is not what He wanted. He created the world to make known to us how things are, and He wanted a person like us who would learn *Chassidus* (the teachings of Chassidism) like this: learn the *seder hishtalshelus* (the order of the chain of worlds) and from it get to the original thing before. For that He had to make the levels, but what He wanted was only the end. "We were the intrinsic, and that whole other business is extrinsic. It was just created for us."

blocks.title: The ground and the sun
blocks.text: He wanted people, not a ground or a sun; but to have us He had to have a ground and a sun. Why? He could have had us floating in space. But He wanted us doing certain mitzvos that have to do with the ground and the sun. Still, the real thing He wanted was us.

sections.title: The answer: the will "from before You" never changes
sections.summary: He wants one thing, before and after. What changes is only what that will is dressed in: candy or shouting, brown walls or pink. "May it be Your will" asks for a change in the doing, in *Asiya*, and it leans on the will that does not change. He is literally here, exactly as before the world was created.

phrases.he: ועפ"ז יתורץ הכל דמה שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי בין רצון של חסד או דין בכל עולם דאבי''ע היינו כמו שהוא קודם הצמצום ומסך שבוקע בו ונעשה כתר לעולם התחתון
ועל זה אמר יהי רצון
מלפניך דייקא
phrases.en: From You.

blocks.title: The father: candy one minute, shouting the next
blocks.text: He wants one certain thing. A father gives his kid candy one minute and shouts at him the next. What is he changing? "I didn't change nothing. I want my kid to succeed." If a candy will help him study, he gives him a candy; if he needs to shout at him so he studies, he shouts at him. Really, nothing changed.

blocks.question: But in "May it be Your will" we are saying that we change the will.
blocks.text: That too is not really a change, not even in the *ratzon*. The *Aibershter* wanted a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below): a house with His wife, with the Jews, *Knesses Yisroel* (the community of Israel).

blocks.title: The house, the pool table and the pink walls
blocks.text:
A man builds a house for his wife: brown walls, and a pool table in the basement. What does she need a pool table for? She wants pink walls, and a lounge in the basement for all her friends, with hair dryers. He runs back to the architect, who asks whether he changed his mind: wasn't he a guy who never changes, *Ani Havaya lo shanisi*? "I didn't change nothing. I wanted to make my wife happy." Brown walls or pink walls, he doesn't care; that is what he wanted before and what he wants now. So what changed?

Only the external things the will is dressed in changed. So his wife can say *yehi ratzon milfanecha*: change this will for a pool table into a will for what she wants. And so can we: He really wanted to make His wife happy.

*Milfanecha* precisely: **from You**. The *ratzon* for what kind of wall did change, from brown to pink. But the *ratzon milfanecha*, the will from before You, is exactly the same: he wanted to keep his wife happy.

phrases.he: וכל בחינת מעלה ומטה שבעולם זה שוין כו'
phrases.en: And the whole up and down is all exactly the same as far as He's concerned.

phrases.he: אבל אחר הצמצום נמשך הרצון בחכמה ומדות בשינויים
phrases.en: Then it comes with *shinuyim*.

phrases.he: עד מלכות דעשיה, אומרים יהי רצון מלפניך, בשינוי לענין עשיה בפועל ממש, מדין לחסד וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין:

blocks.text: Up and down are exactly the same as far as He is concerned. After the *tzimtzum* the will comes **with *shinuyim***: a *ratzon* for pink walls, a *ratzon* for green walls. The wife does not want him to change his will so that he stops loving her. Just the opposite: "that's what she's playing on." She wants the *ratzon* for the *asiya*, for what is done, to change.

"This is actually the hardest chapter of the whole book." Other chapters are more intricate and harder to follow, but this one is the hardest to understand, and it is the actual point of the whole book. Not chapters like seven and eight, with the general picture and all the unifications of the *Kesarim* (crowns), of *chachma* and the *middos*, but this one, before chapter 10: *Ani Havaya lo shanisi*, I have not changed.

"I have not changed" does not mean only that this world is a garment with the *Aibershter* hidden inside. There is literally no change at all: the *Aibershter* is literally here with us, exactly as "You are He before the world was created." The *tzimtzum* changes nothing, because the *Aibershter* Himself is higher than both spreading forth and *tzimtzum*. On the contrary: the *tzimtzum* is how it is that it does not change.

As the text will explain later, the power of the *tzimtzum* is itself an infinite power of the *Atzmus*. By Him, to open and to close are the same power, and closing is almost the higher one. "It's no *chachma* (wisdom) to be an infinite light in an infinite light. But to be an infinite light in a finite world is a bigger *chachma*."

blocks.title: The last of three thousand meshalim
blocks.text: Shlomo HaMelech made three thousand *meshalim* (analogies). It is *davka* the last *mashal*, that he was able to put it into so low a *mashal*, which is the highest *chachma*. And this world is a last *mashal*.

blocks.title: What a small child thinks
blocks.text: The point of the whole book: the *Aibershter* is literally here. That is the *daas* (knowledge) of a small child, who thinks the *Aibershter* is *mamash* standing here with us. Why can't we see Him? Because He is invisible. A *maamar* (discourse) of the Mitteler Rebbe says this is so close to the truth that it is *mamash* the truth. Like those angels: they were there, only the man could not see them.

Everything we do and everything that happens is literally the encompassing light, the inner light and the *Atzmus* of the *Aibershter*, all here. The *tzimtzum* makes no difference: darkness is as light; revealed or hidden is exactly the same to Him. That is why this is the hardest chapter, and all the chapters that follow are basically the *pratim* (particulars) of this one.

Chapter nine: the ninth of Kislev is the Mitteler Rebbe's birthday and *yahrtzeit* (the anniversary of his passing). The class is on the fourth of Kislev, in the Mitteler Rebbe's week, which builds up to the ninth and tenth of Kislev, his days. A very special week.

reviewQuestions.question: What are the forms of the question the chapter opens with, and what do they share?
Why would a flow by cause and effect mean a change in the Essence, and why does a light not?
Where does the projector stop being a good picture of the *tzimtzum*, and what does the television add?
How do Bilaam's donkey and the prophet's servant show that the inner light is not lessened below?
What does "at first it arose in thought to create with the attribute of judgement" mean, if it was not a mistake?
When we say "May it be Your will", which will are we asking to change, and which will are we relying on?
